newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end down, U.S. attack scares players.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end down, U.S. attack scares players.

text.p: ** (1000 GMT) Bombay shares tumble as U.S. attack on Iraq unnerves players
** Finance Minister puts off statement on budget, market disappointed
** Institutional funds stay away, punters drive prices down
** Benchmark Bombay index falls 76.32 points, or 2.14 percent, to 3,486.66 provisional close
Share prices fell broadly on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday after the U.S. attack on Iraq jolted the market, brokers said.
"That was the only reason for the crash," said Kamlesh Sanghavi, director at Sanghavi Savla Stock Brokers Ltd. "People were taken by surprise."
Traders said the tumble was a "knee-jerk" reaction to the Middle-East crisis.
"The initial reaction was bad. We should see some discounting in a couple of days when the fears recede," said Ram Mohan at Lloyds Brokerage.
The setback came after the market started strongly in anticipation of a crucial speech by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in parliament about the budget proposals.
Shortly before close Chidambaram put off his statement because of a disruption in parliament, and brokers said they were disappointed but hopeful.
"To a certain extent I'm disappointed but this will keep expectations afloat," Sanghavi said.
Analysts said the Middle-East flare up drove foreign institutional buyers to the sidelines and local punters pounded the market.
"This news (the U.S. attack) has spoiled the party," said broker Ashok Khandwala. "We don't know what will happen. It's worrying. I think prices will go down."
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index fell 13.64 points to a provisional 1,023.36.
TELCO fell 21 rupees to 501, ACC 49.25 to 2,163, Nestle 13.0 to 261, Hind Lever 15 to 812, BSES 7.50 to 197.50, Tata Power 6.0 to 150.75 and Grasim 9.50 to 434.50.
SBI and TISCO each dropped 6.50 rupees, to 276.25 and 193.50 respectively while Reliance eased 7.25 to 207.25.
